children: President Donald Trump spared Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh any flack for raising interest rates Wednesday, instead blaming what he called a "hostile" and "political" Fed board.
"I'm relying on Kevin, but he has got a very tough board," Trump told reporters Wednesday evening.

Notably, Warsh voted alongside all the other Federal Open Market Committee members to raise interest rates earlier in the day. At a news conference, Warsh repeatedly said the rate increase was needed to quell above-target inflation.
"Stable prices have been the problem for now more than five and a half years," Warsh said.
But Trump didn't blame Warsh, who he appointed to replace Jerome Powell. During Powell's tenure as chair, Trump often directly attacked him for not lowering rates.

"I told Kevin, I said, 'You might as well vote with the board because it's just not going to matter,'" Trump said. "He has got a board that was put there by a lot of other people, and the interest rates are too high. They're not appropriate."
Trump also accused the FOMC of raising interest rates to hurt him politically. The economy and affordability are top concerns for voters ahead of the November midterm election.
"They're raising that only for political reasons, and that's a raise against Trump," he said. "They are raising the rates to make Trump do as bad as he can possibly do."
Trump posted on Truth Social after Warsh's news conference that interest rates should be 1% or less because the U.S. is the "best credit in the world-BY FAR."

Speaking to press Wednesday evening, he reiterated that: "We should be paying the lowest interest rate anywhere in the world because we have the strongest credit. If we wanted to get rid of deficits, which we could do with the swipe of the pen with every country, we'd make a trillion and a half dollars a year. We'd pay off our debt. We'd do all sorts of things. But we haven't chosen to do that. But at some point, we will. Interest rates are too high."
